questions.title: PELT Gaussian mean-shift segmentation from paper to code
questions.description: Focused L2 paper-to-code evaluation based on Killick, Fearnhead, and Eckley, Optimal detection of changepoints with a linear computational cost, JASA 107(500), 2012. The model-visible snapshot contains the exact arXiv v1 LaTeX source and bibliography; package implementations and gold outcomes are withheld from runtime. For a finite univariate signal, develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace that defines the additive penalized segmentation objective, Gaussian mean-shift residual-sum-of-squares segment cost, dynamic-programming recursion, backtracking, and PELT pruning theorem. Derive O(1) segment costs from prefix sums. State the cost condition and pruning constant needed for exactness, distinguish global optimality from binary-segmentation heuristics, and distinguish the paper's conditional expected-linear result from a universal worst-case linear-time claim. Explain the minimum-segment-length feasible set, including why a pruning witness at endpoint t cannot remove an earlier candidate for a future endpoint until a segment beginning at t is itself feasible. Explain the F(0)=-beta convention that charges beta per changepoint rather than per segment, deterministic tie handling, and the location-shift, joint-rescaling, and time-reversal equivariances. The required model-authored artifact is est_pelt_gaussian_mean and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract as Python source using the paper's exact pruned dynamic program. Exploratory Python may test recursions and compare exhaustive small-n partitions. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses n=240, minimum segment length 10, penalty 3*log(240), at least 1000 fresh replicates per design, and one seed per design frozen before outcomes. The null design is iid N(0,1). The one-change design has means 0 and 2.5 on two consecutive length-120 segments with unit variance. The three-change design has means 0, 2, -2, and 1.5 on four consecutive length-60 segments with unit variance. Null success means no changepoint; one-change success means exactly one changepoint within five observations of 120; three-change success means exactly three changepoints, each within five observations of 60, 120, and 180. The lower two-Monte-Carlo-standard-error success bound must be at least 0.95 for the null and one-change designs and at least 0.90 for the three-change design. These finite simulations assess executable behavior under one public penalty and three public Gaussian designs only; they do not prove universal consistency, optimal penalty selection, expected-linear complexity, or performance under other costs, variances, dimensions, or dependence. Exact source-code replication, unknown-variance likelihood calibration, alternative cost models, online detection, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable. Unresolved mathematical, ABI, execution, complexity, or empirical gaps must remain explicit.

primary_paper.title: Optimal detection of changepoints with a linear computational cost
primary_paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

request_fields.name: signal
request_fields.meaning: The univariate observations in time order.
request_fields.shape: One vector with 4 through 512 finite non-Boolean entries, each in [-1e6, 1e6].
request_fields.indexing: signal[i] is observation i in zero-based Python order; a changepoint k separates signal[0:k] from signal[k:n].
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, string, null, object, nested, empty, nonfinite, below-domain, or above-domain values rather than coercing, dropping, flattening, clipping, or truncating them.

request_fields.name: penalty
request_fields.meaning: The strictly positive beta charged for every reported changepoint.
request_fields.indexing: One value shared by all candidate segments in the request.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, string, null, object, array, nonfinite, zero, negative, or above-domain values rather than coercing, taking an absolute value, clipping, or substituting a default.

request_fields.name: min_segment_length
request_fields.meaning: The minimum number of observations in every segment, including the first and last.
request_fields.shape: One finite non-Boolean integer from 1 through floor(n/2).
request_fields.indexing: A boundary sequence is feasible only when each successive segment length is at least this value.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, string, null, object, array, noninteger, nonfinite, below-domain, or infeasible values rather than coercing, rounding, clipping, or substituting a default.

response_fields.name: changepoints
response_fields.meaning: The exact globally minimizing internal segment boundaries.
response_fields.shape: A possibly empty strictly increasing array of finite non-Boolean integers.
response_fields.indexing: Each k denotes a split between signal[k-1] and signal[k]; 0 and n are excluded, and the terminal n is not returned.
response_fields.edge_cases: Every implied segment must satisfy min_segment_length. Among partitions with exactly equal computed objective, return the lexicographically smallest changepoint array.
response_fields.normalization: Minimize the declared residual-sum-of-squares plus penalty-times-number-of-changepoints objective over the complete feasible partition set.

response_fields.name: objective
response_fields.meaning: The penalized objective attained by the returned changepoints.
response_fields.indexing: One value for the complete signal and returned partition.
response_fields.edge_cases: Return the unrounded finite value; do not omit the changepoint penalty, charge the first segment, normalize by segment length, estimate a variance, or return an information criterion.
response_fields.normalization: objective=sum over segments of sum_{i in segment}(signal_i-segment_mean)^2 + penalty*len(changepoints).

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly signal, penalty, and min_segment_length, and the response contains exactly changepoints and objective. Missing, extra, malformed, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values are rejected rather than ignored or coerced.

Use the paper's additive dynamic-programming recursion with F(0)=-penalty and valid PELT pruning for the Gaussian residual-sum-of-squares cost. With a positive minimum segment length, do not remove a candidate using a pruning witness until the witness can begin a feasible following segment. The returned feasible partition is a global minimizer; greedy, binary-segmentation, local-search, thresholding, and approximate-grid substitutes are out of scope.
Repeated calls with the same request return the same JSON value and do not mutate the request, use random state, access files, invoke subprocesses, or use the network.

Adding one constant to every signal value leaves changepoints and objective unchanged up to floating roundoff. Multiplying every signal value by a finite nonzero factor a while multiplying penalty by a^2 leaves changepoints unchanged and multiplies objective by a^2.
Reversing a length-n signal maps each changepoint k to n-k, sorted increasingly, and leaves the objective unchanged up to floating roundoff.

Prefix sums provide O(1) Gaussian segment costs and PELT prunes candidate last changepoints without changing the exact optimum. The implementation and report must not turn the paper's conditional expected-linear result into a universal worst-case linear guarantee.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze n=240, min_segment_length=10, penalty=3*log(240), the three declared unit-variance Gaussian designs, at least 1000 fresh replicates per design, one fresh seed per design, exact estimator invocation, success indicators, Monte Carlo standard errors, and one-sided lower two-standard-error decision rules.
For iid N(0,1), success is an empty changepoint array and the success rate minus two Monte Carlo standard errors is at least 0.95.

For consecutive length-120 segments with means 0 and 2.5, success is exactly one changepoint within five observations of 120 and the success rate minus two Monte Carlo standard errors is at least 0.95.

For consecutive length-60 segments with means 0, 2, -2, and 1.5, success is exactly three changepoints, respectively within five observations of 60, 120, and 180, and the success rate minus two Monte Carlo standard errors is at least 0.90.

The confirmatory assessment tests executable behavior under one finite protocol only. It is not proof of global optimality, universal consistency, penalty optimality, expected-linear complexity, or performance outside the three declared Gaussian designs.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: For every valid bounded request, run_estimator performs finite prefix-sum, dynamic-programming, PELT-pruning, and backtracking operations and returns exactly one response without randomization, file access, network access, subprocesses, or request mutation.
